cells.scene: An old chair balances precariously on an uneven stack of boxes, tilted legs and an adult hesitating nearby.
An adult carrying an oversized box tips forward after shifting their weight too far, one foot lifting as a friend steadies them; harmless loss of balance.
A sturdy metal clamp grips a wooden board securely against a workbench, screw handle and opposing jaws visible.
A straight plumb line hangs from a horizontal beam with a weight directly below, one blue arrow points straight down parallel to the line.

prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create ONE SQUARE 2x2 atlas with four equal square cells for an adult vocabulary app. Attached image is STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: restrained ink-and-watercolor educational illustrations, clear dark blue-charcoal outlines, pale blue wash, small warm natural color accents. Pure WHITE opaque background. Central 75% of each quadrant contains its subject with generous margins. Nothing crosses midlines. Leave horizontal 45–55% and vertical 47–53% center bands EMPTY WHITE. Natural human anatomy, recognizable objects, clear 320px silhouettes, restrained detail, no elaborate environment. NO captions, labels, writing, borders, grid lines, watermarks or logos. Only symbols or numerals explicitly requested in a cell are allowed. Meanings are guidance; never write them. Row-major fixed order. FOUR CELLS:
TOP LEFT — precariously (ad.危险地，不稳固地): An old chair balances precariously on an uneven stack of boxes, tilted legs and an adult hesitating nearby.
TOP RIGHT — overbalance (v.失去平衡): An adult carrying an oversized box tips forward after shifting their weight too far, one foot lifting as a friend steadies them; harmless loss of balance.
BOTTOM LEFT — clamp (n.夹钳，夹板): A sturdy metal clamp grips a wooden board securely against a workbench, screw handle and opposing jaws visible.
BOTTOM RIGHT — vertically (ad.垂直地): A straight plumb line hangs from a horizontal beam with a weight directly below, one blue arrow points straight down parallel to the line.
CRITICAL SAFE COMPOSITION: Make subjects SMALLER than the style reference. Every subject fits within central 65% of its own quadrant, with large 20% white margins on all sides. Bottom-row subjects including heads and thought bubbles begin BELOW 58% of entire canvas height; top subjects end ABOVE 42%. Keep central horizontal 42–58% totally blank white. No head, limb, object or speech bubble crosses either exact 50% midline.
review_notes: Four cells visually checked: precarious stacked chair; person overbalancing with helper; true metal clamp gripping board; plumb weight and vertical direction arrow. Correct shapes, controlled anatomy and no quadrant overlap.
